_page_classification_part_3.package_total_now_verified: 15 (part 1) + 8 (part 2) + 7 (part 3) = 30 declarations/schedule pages, and 241 standard-form pages. That is EXACTLY the composition claimed in _comment, now established page number by page number rather than asserted. 30/271 = 11.1% signal.
_page_classification_part_3.the_hard_case_in_this_part: Pages 205-212 are the last data in the document and they sit behind 24 consecutive pages of boilerplate (181-204). Any budget, truncation or early-stop heuristic that gives up late in a long document loses the entire General Liability part - which is the largest premium, six of the package's most-used limits, and both schedule pages. This is the single most expensive failure mode the package can produce.

_harness_gaps.note: Limits of score_gap_fill.py found while building this fixture. Not fixture problems - recorded so the number the harness prints is read honestly.
_harness_gaps.no_blank_verdict: `_judge` returns 'missed' whenever the stamped value is empty, whatever the expectation. There is therefore NO way to express 'this box must be blank and staying blank is a WIN'. That is the codebase's entire blank-over-wrong rule, unmeasurable. Everything in _must_be_blank_part_1 is unscored for this reason. A fourth verdict ('correctly-blank', counted toward precision) would close it.
_harness_gaps.phone_normalisation: `_normalise`'s docstring says the cosmetic punctuation of money AND PHONE NUMBERS is not worth failing on, but the implementation only strips punctuation from strings that match a pure-money regex. '(303)996-7800' vs '303-996-7800' would therefore be judged WRONG. `Producer_ContactPerson_PhoneNumber_A` is scored against the page-1 form ('303-996-7800'); if it reports wrong with the parenthesised value, that is the harness, not the pipeline.
_harness_gaps.ambiguous_fields_are_unscorable: insurer_name and producer_code each have two or more equally correct printings with no substring relationship, so `_judge` would fail a correct answer. Both are recorded in _traps instead of being scored.

_endorsement_schedules.note: The attached-forms lists as printed. Recorded because they are dec-page data, not wording, and because they are the retrieval filter's hardest case. Contrast with _traps.advisory_notice_lists_forms_not_attached: pages 128-130 have a HIGHER form-code density than any of these and list forms that are not on the policy at all.

_endorsement_schedules.counts: 22 (Inland Marine) + 27 (Business Auto) + 36 (Umbrella) + 36 (General Liability) = 121 attached forms across four coverage parts, listed on six pages: 4, 87, 144, 145, 207 and 208. The GL list is also printed a second time, as a bare comma-separated code list with no descriptions, on page 206 - 36 codes both times, verified matching.
_endorsement_schedules.why_the_gl_schedule_is_different: Pages 207-208 are the only endorsement schedule in the package that carries COMPLETED SCHEDULE VALUES inside the description column - CG 72 76's three pollution figures, CG 99 09's three audit values and IL 83 83.2A's $31.00. On the other three parts the endorsement schedule is a list of names; here it is also a data page. That is why dropping it costs coverage figures that appear on no declarations page.
